subject.title: perf(slack): remove structural channel-side latency (serial prepare, global write cap, unbounded thread pagination)

question: Should this PR keep Slack write-client serialization until non-send write helpers have equivalent per-target ordering, or should maintainers accept uncapped SDK concurrency for edits, reactions, pins, and deletes?
rationale: The PR reverses a shipped ordering safeguard, and the proposed replacement queue does not cover every current write-client caller.

options.title: Serialize all writes before merge
options.body: Keep the cap or add per-target ordering around action and draft write helpers, then prove sends, edits, reactions, pins, and deletes still behave correctly.

options.title: Accept uncapped non-send writes
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept SDK default concurrency for non-send Slack writes if latency is worth the ordering and burst-limit tradeoff.

options.title: Split write-cap removal out
options.body: Land the prepare/thread-history latency work now and revisit write concurrency in a separate PR with focused ordering proof.

recommendation.title: Serialize all writes before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the cap or add per-target ordering around action and draft write helpers, then prove sends, edits, reactions, pins, and deletes still behave correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the prior Slack ordering safeguard this PR proposes to remove.
